notes:
POC summary + call notes:
- PRIMARY ISSUE: p95 latency / streaming tail. Customer requires ~200ms p95 for chat message streaming across sessions. Our hosted baseline: p95 spikes between 420-600ms under realistic workload (variable seq lengths). Dedicated trial (4xA100) improved tail to ~280-380ms but still misses target for interactive experience.
- What we tried: kernel selection tweaks, lower batch sizes for streaming, aggressive KV prefix caching, model quantization (Q4_8) candidate. SE (Priya) ran internal perf traces — identified long-tail stalls on KV cache evictions and background model page-ins for rare tokens.
- Customer feedback: "can't risk user-facing stalls — we'll lose customers if chat lags or stalls mid-response." (VP Product).
- Competitive pressure: VeloServe claims sub-200ms p95 via edge shard routing + distilled micro-models; Cobalt team is running parallel trial.
- Org risk: CTO who championed the project left after reorg; replacement is focused on infrastructure cost cuts. Procurement has paused new platform spends (internal memo).
- Security: no blocker — SAML/KMS/audit ok. Not deciding on security grounds.
- Commercial: ARR estimate $100-250k; willing to consider dedicated contract if SLOs met.
- Current account status: stalled -> customer unresponsive since 2026-02-25; likely closed-lost to VeloServe or deferred by budget freeze. Recommend internal win/loss and technical post-mortem focused on streaming tail.
- Suggested engineering follow-ups (internal): reproduce long-tail KV eviction at scale; prototype edge routing shim to reduce in-region hop; test micro-model distillation path as a fallback for low-latency sessions.
- Suggested commercial follow-ups: offer limited-risk pilot (SLA credits) or hybrid routing A/B with VeloServe-like edge fallback; escalate only if customer re-engages.
- Quote from meeting: "If streaming doesn't feel instant, product team won't ship this feature" — former CTO.
